baseline.conditions: Basalt freight terraces; gas closure adds a day.

title: The freight that went uphill
daily_life: Cinder Cuts and Kettle Crown share a history of unequal transport decisions. A new contract can provide real work while still asking the poorer terraces to absorb risk.
timing: Three days covers the basalt freight terraces. A gas closure adds one day only for the established limited closure scenario; persistent unsafe conditions mean an indefinite hold.
handoff: Local crews check the proposed departure, not an abstract daily quota. A clearance from yesterday does not establish the state of a vent today.
story_option: A clean forge yard sends its waste downhill, drawing ashmaws toward another neighborhood. The apparent animal problem points back to a disposal decision.
production: Ashmaws tolerate hot ground, not liquid lava. Keep safe civic terraces, gas troughs and raider storage geographically distinct.
direction: Listed a-to-b planning reference; reverse passage requires a fresh itinerary.
geometry: Regional endpoints and route length inherited; connecting line is not a surveyed track.
